children: Raw sugar futures on ICE steadied on Thursday after hitting a one-week high earlier, while arabica coffee headed back toward a three-month low.
SUGAR
* Raw sugar
settled down 0.17 cent, or 1%, at 17.58 cents per lb, having touched 18.02 cents/lb earlier in the session.

* Sugar production in top grower Brazil's key center-south region is forecast to have declined by 42.5% in the first half of September after rain disrupted harvesting, according to a survey of 10 analysts published by the S&P Global team late on Wednesday.

* "We are seeing more rain-related crush delays (in Brazil) and there is more rain expected in the first week of October. The market might still test 18.60," said independent broker and consultant Michael McDougall.
* He also noted that rising oil prices are driving sugar higher but added that demand remains weak.

* India, for example, is moving closer to new regulations to restrict the sale of foods high in fat and sugar within a 50-metre radius of schools, the latest proposal to cut the consumption of junk food in the country.
* White sugar
rose 0.8% to $509.90 a metric ton.
COFFEE
* Arabica coffee
settled down 0.55 cent, or 0.2%, at $2.7535 per lb, heading back toward Tuesday's three-month low of $2.6300.

* Top grower Brazil's 2026 coffee crop is expected to total a record 67.6 million 60-kg bags, national crop agency Conab said, raising its estimate from 66.7 million as stronger arabica yields more than offset lower robusta production.

* "Uncertainty remains around what a super El Niño could mean for bean fill in Brazil, and around the dry conditions it typically brings to Indonesia," Cardiff Coffee Trading said in a note, adding that conditions remain satisfactory for now.
* Robusta coffee
fell 0.8% to $3,290 a ton after slumping to a 3-1/2-month low of $3,218 on Tuesday.
* "Healthy supplies from Brazil and steadily rising exports from Vietnam are putting pressure on robusta prices," said a trader based in top robusta grower Vietnam.
COCOA
* London cocoa
​settled up £55, or 1.3%, at £4,183  per ton​.
* No. 2 cocoa grower Ghana will open its 2026/27 cocoa season on Friday and announce the farmgate price for the season, five sources told Reuters.
* Broker ADMIS said rains are expected to continue over the next 10 days in top grower West Africa, easing concerns over the upcoming 2026/27 crop.
* New York cocoa
rose 1.1% to $5,590 a ton.
